headline: Over 5 lakh fail as SSC pass rate hits 19-year low
summary: The overall pass rate for 9 general education boards dropped to 64.05%, with English and Mathematics being the primary hurdles for students.
details: The pass rate for the SSC examinations across 9 general education boards has fallen to 64.05%, the lowest in 19 years. Out of 1,404,539 candidates, 899,610 passed while 504,929 failed, meaning more than one-third of the students did not qualify.

The decline is largely attributed to poor performance in English and Mathematics, which are compulsory subjects. In eight of the nine boards, the pass rate for English was below 80%, with Mymensingh and Sylhet boards showing particularly low results.

Girls continued to outperform boys for the 11th consecutive year. Female students had a pass rate of approximately 68%, compared to 60% for boys. Girls also led in achieving GPA-5, with over 58,000 girls securing the top grade compared to 47,000 boys.
The Humanities group saw the lowest pass rates, with only 41% of boys and 54% of girls passing. In contrast, the Science group performed better, with pass rates of 77% for boys and 84% for girls.

Concerns have been raised over the quality of education, as 57 educational institutions saw a 100% failure rate this year, up from 48 last year. Educationists suggest that the results highlight a systemic failure in learning standards and teacher availability.

The number of students achieving GPA-5 has also decreased, with 106,009 students securing the top grade this year, compared to 125,180 last year. The Dhaka board topped both the pass rate and GPA-5 rankings, while Mymensingh board lagged behind.
caption:
More than 5 lakh students failed their SSC exams this year, marking the lowest pass rate in nearly two decades.

The pass rate for the SSC examinations across 9 general education boards has fallen to 64.05%, the lowest in 19 years. Out of 1,404,539 candidates, 899,610 passed while 504,929 failed, meaning more than one-third of the students did not qualify.

The decline is largely attributed to poor performance in English and Mathematics, which are compulsory subjects. In eight of the nine boards, the pass rate for English was below 80%, with Mymensingh and Sylhet boards showing particularly low results.

Girls continued to outperform boys for the 11th consecutive year. Female students had a pass rate of approximately 68%, compared to 60% for boys. Girls also led in achieving GPA-5, with over 58,000 girls securing the top grade compared to 47,000 boys.

The Humanities group saw the lowest pass rates, with only 41% of boys and 54% of girls passing. In contrast, the Science group performed better, with pass rates of 77% for boys and 84% for girls.

Concerns have been raised over the quality of education, as 57 educational institutions saw a 100% failure rate this year, up from 48 last year. Educationists suggest that the results highlight a systemic failure in learning standards and teacher availability.

The number of students achieving GPA-5 has also decreased, with 106,009 students securing the top grade this year, compared to 125,180 last year. The Dhaka board topped both the pass rate and GPA-5 rankings, while Mymensingh board lagged behind.

headline: Tk 1.21 crore robbed from Uttara fuel pump in broad daylight
summary: Armed robbers stole a massive sum from a filling station owned by the Prime Minister's cousin in Dhaka.
details: Armed robbers stole Tk 1.21 crore from a fuel pump in the Uttara area of Dhaka in broad daylight.
The robbers targeted a filling station owned by the cousin of the Prime Minister.
During the heist, a filling station official was hacked, leaving him injured.
The attackers carried out the robbery with speed and precision, escaping the scene before authorities could intervene.
Police have launched an investigation to track down the suspects and recover the stolen funds.
caption:

The attackers carried out the robbery with speed and precision, escaping the scene before authorities could intervene.

Police have launched an investigation to track down the suspects and recover the stolen funds.
